title: Bobotie (Cape Malay spiced baked mince with an egg custard topping)

ingredients.name: white bread, soaked in 200 ml milk

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Fry the onions in the oil until golden, then stir in the curry powder and turmeric for a minute.
Add the mince and brown it well, breaking up lumps with a spoon.
Squeeze the milk out of the soaked bread (keep the milk) and crumble the bread into the mince along with the jam, vinegar, raisins, almonds, salt and pepper.
Mix well and spoon into a greased baking dish, pressing it down evenly. Tuck the bay leaves into the surface.
Beat the eggs with the 150 ml of milk and the reserved bread milk and pour over the meat.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is set and lightly golden.
Serve with yellow rice, chutney and a tomato and onion salad.

title: Boeber (Cape Malay vermicelli and sago milk pudding)
steps: Soak the sago in a little water for 10 minutes and drain.
Warm the milk with the cardamom and cinnamon stick over low heat for 10 minutes without boiling.
Add the sago and vermicelli and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sago turns clear and the vermicelli is soft.
Stir in the sugar, sultanas and almonds and cook for another 3 minutes.
Remove the spices, stir in the rose water and serve warm in cups or bowls. It is traditionally made on the 15th night of Ramadan.

title: Braaibroodjie (grilled cheese, tomato and onion sandwich)
steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
On the unbuttered side of four slices, layer the cheese, tomato, onion and a spoonful of chutney, seasoning lightly.
Top each with another slice, buttered side facing out, and press down.
Place in a hinged grill, over hot coals or in a hot pan, and toast for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut in half and eat while hot, usually alongside grilled meat.

title: Bunny chow (Durban curry served in a hollowed-out loaf)

ingredients.name: curry powder (Durban-style masala if you can find it)
unsliced white loaf (about 800 g), cut into 4 quarters

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onions until deep golden.
Add the cinnamon stick and curry leaves, stir for 30 seconds, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook for a minute.
Add the lamb and brown on all sides, then add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Pour in the water, add salt, cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for another 25 to 30 minutes until the lamb is tender and the sauce thick.
Cut a deep well in each loaf quarter, keep the removed bread crumb, and fill the loaves with curry.
Top with coriander and eat with your hands, using the bread crumb to scoop up the sauce.

title: Frikkadel (Afrikaner baked meatballs)

ingredients.name: minced beef (or half beef, half pork)
white bread, soaked in a little milk

steps: Heat the oven to 190 C and grease a baking dish.
Squeeze the excess milk from the bread and crumble it into a bowl with the mince, onion, egg, vinegar, coriander, nutmeg, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Mix thoroughly with your hands until combined, then shape into 12 firm balls.
Place the meatballs in the dish, drizzle with the oil and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with mashed potato, beetroot salad or chutney, or cold in a sandwich.

title: Gatsby (Cape Town long sandwich of masala steak and chips)

ingredients.name: long soft bread rolls (about 30 cm), or 1 baguette cut in two
beef rump or sirloin, in thin strips

steps: Toss the beef strips with the masala, oil and a pinch of salt and let them sit for 15 minutes.
Fry the strips in a very hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes until browned and just cooked.
Split the rolls lengthways, spread with mayonnaise and chutney and layer lettuce, tomato and onion.
Fill with the masala steak and pile hot chips on top, pressing them in lightly.
Cut each roll into portions to share and eat while warm.

title: Hertzoggie (jam tartlets topped with coconut meringue)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Cream the butter and 60 g sugar, beat in the egg yolks, then mix in the flour and baking powder to form a soft dough.
Press the dough into the tin holes to make small cups, prick the bases and bake for 8 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Put a half spoonful of apricot jam into each pastry case.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, gradually beating in 100 g sugar until glossy, then fold in the coconut.
Spoon the meringue over the jam, bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden, cool in the tin and then lift out.

title: Isidudu (soft Xhosa and Zulu maize-meal porridge)
steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a pot.
Mix about a third of the maize meal with 100 ml of cold water to a paste and stir it into the boiling water.
Slowly add the rest of the maize meal in a thin stream, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is soft and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and serve with butter, sugar and cold or warm milk. Some families prefer it with a little vinegar and sugar.

title: Kota (Soweto quarter-loaf filled with chips, sausage and atchar)

ingredients.name: quarter loaves of unsliced white bread (each about 200 g)
tomato sauce or chakalaka to taste

steps: Scoop out most of the soft crumb from the middle of each quarter loaf, leaving a sturdy shell and keeping the crumb aside.
Place a slice of cheese in the bottom of each shell and add a layer of hot chips.
Add the sliced sausages, polony or ham, and a fried egg to each.
Spoon over the atchar and a drizzle of tomato sauce or chakalaka.
Top with more chips and press the reserved crumb on top as a lid. Eat it straight away, with your hands.

title: Malva pudding (South African apricot jam sponge with hot cream sauce)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a 20 cm baking dish.
Beat the eggs and sugar until pale and thick, then beat in the jam, melted butter and vinegar.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda in the milk. Alternately fold the flour with a pinch of salt and the milk mixture into the egg mixture until smooth.
Pour into the dish and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until risen, dark golden and springy.
While it bakes, heat the cream, butter, sugar and hot water in a saucepan, stirring until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot sauce over the pudding as soon as it comes from the oven and let it soak in for 10 minutes. Serve warm with custard or ice cream.

title: Mealie bread (sweetcorn bread)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a loaf tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat the eggs with the milk and melted butter, then stir in the creamed sweetcorn.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for a few minutes and serve warm with butter, as a side with a braai or soup.

title: Melktert (Cape milk tart)
steps: For the pastry, rub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder and 50 g sugar, then mix in the egg to form a dough. Chill for 30 minutes, roll it out and line a 23 cm tart tin. Heat the oven to 180 C.
Prick the base, line with baking paper and baking beans and blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 more minutes.
Heat 650 ml of the milk with the cinnamon stick until nearly boiling, then remove the stick.
Whisk the remaining milk with the cornflour, flour, 100 g sugar and egg yolks, and stir into the hot milk. Cook, stirring, until very thick, then take off the heat and add the butter and vanilla.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the custard.
Pour into the baked crust and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until just set. Cool, dust generously with cinnamon and serve at room temperature.

title: Monkey gland sauce (South African sweet and tangy steak sauce)
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the chutney, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, sugar, wine, vinegar and chilli sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy.
Taste and adjust the sweetness, tang or heat. Despite the name, it contains no gland of any kind.
Serve warm over grilled steak or burgers, or with chips or onion rings.

title: Morogo (stewed wild greens with onion and tomato)

ingredients.name: morogo, amaranth leaves or spinach, washed and chopped

steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil, add the greens and blanch for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain and squeeze out the water. Skip this step for spinach.
Heat the oil in a pan, fry the onion until soft, then add the garlic and the chilli.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until soft.
Add the greens and salt, mix well, cover and cook on low for 10 to 15 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with pap, samp or rice.

title: Pampoenkoekies (South African pumpkin fritters)

ingredients.name: cooked and mashed pumpkin (or butternut squash)
sugar mixed with 1 tsp cinnamon, for coating

steps: Mix the mashed pumpkin with the eggs, sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and cinnamon to make a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Drop in heaped tablespoons of batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, roll in the cinnamon sugar and serve warm, optionally with caramel sauce.

title: Potjiekos (South African layered stew cooked in a cast-iron pot)

ingredients.name: beef chuck or stewing beef, cubed

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy cast-iron pot or Dutch oven and brown the beef in batches. Remove it.
Fry the onions and garlic in the same pot until soft, then return the meat and add the bay leaves, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour in the wine and stock, cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour.
Without stirring, layer the carrots, then the potatoes, then the green beans or cabbage on top of the meat.
Cover and cook gently for another 45 to 60 minutes until the meat and vegetables are tender. Do not stir, so the layers stay intact.
Serve straight from the pot with rice, pap or crusty bread.

title: Soetpatats (South African caramelised sweet potatoes)

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into thick slices

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C.
Layer the sweet potato slices in a baking dish or cast-iron pot.
Melt the butter with the sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice, water and salt, stirring until the sugar dissolves, and pour it over the potatoes.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for another 20 to 25 minutes, basting once or twice, until tender and sticky.
Serve hot as a side with roast meat or grilled fish.

title: Sosatie (Cape Malay curried lamb and apricot skewers)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until soft, add the garlic and curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the sugar, vinegar, jam and salt and simmer for 5 minutes. Let the marinade cool completely.
Put the lamb cubes in a dish, pour over the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, ideally overnight.
Soak wooden skewers in water. Thread the meat onto the skewers, alternating with dried apricots.
Grill over medium-hot coals or on a grill pan for about 12 to 15 minutes, turning and basting with the leftover marinade, until browned and cooked through.
Serve with rice, salad or pap.

title: Umngqusho (Xhosa samp and sugar bean stew)

ingredients.name: samp (dried hulled maize kernels), soaked overnight
sugar beans (or pinto beans), soaked overnight

steps: Drain the soaked samp and beans and put them in a large pot with the water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer, partially covered, and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, topping up with hot water when needed.
Meanwhile, soften the onion in half the butter in a small pan and set aside.
When the samp and beans are tender and the mixture is thick, add the salt, onion and remaining butter.
Stir well, mashing a few beans against the pot to thicken it. Serve as a side with grilled chicken or meat, or as a meal on its own.

title: Vetkoek (South African fried bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a large bowl. Add the warm water and mix into a soft, sticky dough.
Knead for 5 minutes, then cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Knock the dough back and divide it into 8 to 10 balls. Rest them for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to about 170 C in a deep pot. Fry the vetkoek in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked inside.
Drain on paper towels. Serve split open and stuffed with curried mince, or with butter and jam, or with cheese and chutney.
